subject.title: Active user message keeps inbound metadata that history strips, breaking prompt-cache byte-stability every turn

question: Should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100272 make the tail runtime-context carrier the permanent fix for active-turn inbound metadata byte-stability?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the linked fix changes compatibility-sensitive prompt/session layout and provider cache-anchor behavior.

options.title: Approve after channel proof
options.body: Require redacted Telegram reply/mention proof or a maintainer-reviewed prompt trace, then merge if exact-head CI is acceptable.

options.title: Accept existing cache proof
options.body: Merge based on the linked provider measurements and focused tests while owning the residual prompt-layout compatibility risk.

options.title: Pause for a different handoff
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers prefer the overlapping runtime-context handoff in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89428 or another narrower design.

recommendation.title: Approve after channel proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Telegram reply/mention proof or a maintainer-reviewed prompt trace, then merge if exact-head CI is acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman merged and maintained the previous prompt-cache boundary work that this issue builds on.
